def-ggm-feasible.title: Feasible generalized least squares
def-ggm-feasible.html:
Let 𝛉𝛉{V(θ):θ∈Θ} be a family of positive definite n×n matrices, Θ⊆Rk, and let 𝛉θ^ be an estimator of 𝛉θ computed from the data. The feasible generalized least squares estimator is 𝛃𝛉𝛉β^F=(X⊤V(θ^)−1X)−1X⊤V(θ^)−1Y,{#eq-ggm-fgls}

for rank(X)=p, with reported covariance matrix 𝛉sF2(X⊤V(θ^)−1X)−1, where sF2 is @eq-ggm-sse evaluated at 𝛉V(θ^).

def-ggm-gls.title: Generalized least squares
def-ggm-gls.html:
Under @eq-ggm-model with V positive definite, a generalized least squares estimate is any 𝛃β^V minimizing QV(b)=(y−Xb)⊤V−1(y−Xb), equivalently any solution of the generalized normal equations X⊤V−1Xb=X⊤V−1y. The fitted vector is 𝛃Xβ^V=AVy, where AV=X(X⊤V−1X)−X⊤V−1{#eq-ggm-gls-projection}

for any generalized inverse, and the generalized residual is 𝛆𝛃ε^V=y−Xβ^V.

eq-ggm-cluster-weights.html: μ^V=∑kwkY¯k∑kwk,wk=mk1−ρ+mkρ,

eq-ggm-equicorr-inverse.html: V−1=11−ρ(I−ρ1+(m−1)ρZZ⊤),

eq-ggm-f.html: F=(SSEV,0−SSEV)/(r−r0)sV2∼F(r−r0,n−r,γ),

eq-ggm-fgls.html: 𝛃𝛉𝛉β^F=(X⊤V(θ^)−1X)−1X⊤V(θ^)−1Y,

eq-ggm-gls-projection.html: AV=X(X⊤V−1X)−X⊤V−1

eq-ggm-model.html: 𝛃E(Y)=Xβ,Cov(Y)=σ2V,

eq-ggm-projection-form.html: 𝛃β~∈argminb∈F(y) (y−Xb)⊤V+(y−Xb)

eq-ggm-quasi.html: ykj ⟼ ykj−cy¯k1−ρ,c=1−1−ρ1+(m−1)ρ,

eq-ggm-rao.html: A=X(X⊤T+X)−X⊤T+

eq-ggm-sse.html: 𝛆𝛆SSEV=ε^V⊤V−1ε^V=Y⊤V−1(I−AV)Y,sV2=SSEVn−r.

eq-ggm-whitened.html: Y∗=V−1/2Y,X∗=V−1/2X.

exm-ggm-balanced.title: Equicorrelation in a balanced layout
exm-ggm-balanced.html:
Let the n=Gm observations fall into G groups of equal size m, let Z be the n×G matrix of group indicators, and let V=(1−ρ)I+ρZZ⊤, the covariance produced by a group-level shock. Since ZZ⊤ is m times the orthogonal projection onto the group-constant vectors, condition (iii) holds iff C(X) is closed under replacing a vector by its group means — which happens whenever C(X) is spanned by group-constant vectors together with vectors whose group means vanish, exactly what a balanced design gives through its between-group and within-group contrasts.

In the El Niño data of @exm-ggm-elnino the groups are years. If the seasonal part of the model is the full set of eleven month effects, every column of X splits into a year-level part and a part whose year means vanish, both again in C(X), so the condition holds exactly: the two fits agree to nine decimals, whatever ρ. Their standard errors do not. At ρ=0.5 the root of the expected reported variance E(s2){(X⊤X)−1}22 is only 0.391 of the true standard error of the trend.

exm-ggm-clusters.title: Unequal clusters
exm-ggm-clusters.html:
Take G clusters of sizes m1,…,mG, a covariate w centred inside every cluster, and the model X=[1,w] with V=(1−ρ)I+ρZZ⊤. Because 1⊤w=0, the vector attached to the slope is c=w/w⊤w, and ZZ⊤w=0 because w has zero mean in each cluster; so Vc=(1−ρ)c∈C(X) and the within-cluster slope is estimated best by ordinary least squares, for every ρ and every set of sizes.

The vector attached to the level is c=1/n, and ZZ⊤1 is the vector whose entry for an observation in cluster k is mk. That step function lies in C(X)=span{1,w} only if all the mk are equal, since w is not constant within clusters. So with unequal clusters the overall level is not estimated best by ordinary least squares; @eq-ggm-cluster-weights gives the estimator that is.

With sizes 2,3,6 and ρ=0.5 the weights of @eq-ggm-cluster-weights are 1.333, 1.500 and 1.714, summing to 4.5476, so the generalized estimate of the level has variance 0.2199σ2 against 0.2479σ2 for the sample mean: an efficiency of 0.887, well above the Kantorovich bound 0.437 that @prp-ggm-ols-loss(c) allows for the eigenvalues 3.500 and 0.500 of this V. The slope loses nothing. Meanwhile the usual standard errors are wrong for both: the root of the expected reported variance is 0.563 of the true standard error for the level and 1.314 of it for the slope.

exm-ggm-effects.title: Regression on estimated treatment effects
exm-ggm-effects.html:
A balanced one-way layout with a treatments and m observations each is analysed, and the estimated effects α^1,…,α^a are reported under the side condition ∑kα^k=0 (@thm-est-side-conditions). A second analyst, with access only to these numbers, regresses them on the dose xk applied to treatment k, fitting E(α^k)=β0+β1xk with an intercept.

The reported vector has 𝛂Cov(α^)=τ2V with V=Ia−11⊤/a and τ2=σ2/m, because α^k=Y¯k−Y¯ and the Y¯k are uncorrelated with variance τ2. Here q=a−1, C(V)=1⊥, and N=1/a. With 1∈C(X) we get d=1 and r=2, so @thm-ggm-singular(b) gives exactly r−d=1 perfectly known function: X⊤N∝(a,∑kxk)⊤, so 𝛃𝛂aβ0+(∑kxk)β1=1⊤Xβ=1⊤α^=0 with probability one. In words: the intercept is determined by the slope, β0=−x¯β1, and the data say so without error. Fitting an intercept was a mistake, and the model itself reveals it.

Everything else is unchanged. Because VX=X−1(1⊤X)/a has columns in C(X), @thm-ggm-ols-blue applies and ordinary least squares is already best: β^1 is the usual centred slope and β^0=−x¯β^1. Since V is idempotent, V+=V and 𝛆𝛆SSEV=ε^⊤ε^ is the usual residual sum of squares, on q−d=a−2 degrees of freedom. What is not unchanged is the covariance matrix. Because 𝛂1⊤α^=0 exactly, Var(β^1)=τ2Sxx,Var(β^0)=x¯2Var(β^1),Cov(β^0,β^1)=−x¯Var(β^1), whereas the ordinary formula s2(X⊤X)−1 reports s2(1/a+x¯2/Sxx) for the intercept. With a=5 doses 0,1,2,4,8, m=6 replicates and σ=1.2, so τ2=0.24, x¯=3.0 and Sxx=40.0: the true variances are 0.00600 for the slope and 0.0540 for the intercept, while the ordinary formula reports 0.1020 on average for the intercept, too large by a factor of 1.89. A simulation of 200,000 layouts reproduces 0.00600 and 0.0540.

exm-ggm-elnino.title: A trend in sea surface temperature
exm-ggm-elnino.title_html: A trend in sea surface temperature
exm-ggm-elnino.html:
The El Niño data record the monthly averaged sea surface temperature of a region of the eastern Pacific for the 61 complete years 1950 to 2010, 732 observations in 61 blocks of 12. Fit a linear trend in time together with three harmonic pairs at one, two and three cycles per year, so p=8. Warm and cold years are warm and cold in every month, so the natural working model is a random annual shock: equicorrelation ρ inside each year, independence across years. Take ρ=0.5 as known for the moment.

Ordinary least squares gives a trend of 0.1349 degrees per decade with the usual standard error 0.0223; generalized least squares gives 0.1347 with standard error 0.0512, larger by a factor of 2.30. The estimates agree to three decimals, the standard errors not at all. The annual cycle tells the same story in reverse: the coefficient of sin⁡(2πmonth/12) is 2.7629 under both fits, with standard error 0.0554 from ordinary and 0.0354 from generalized least squares — this time the usual standard error is too large. Section 31.2 explains both facts.

The F test of “no trend” is 36.7 if the annual shock is ignored and 6.92 once it is allowed for, on 1 and 724 degrees of freedom (p=0.0087): still clear evidence, but with a tenth of the apparent weight. The test that the second and third harmonics are absent moves the other way, from 10.4 to 25.6, because the annual shock inflates s2 and so deflates every F whose numerator lives inside years. Figure 31.1.1(a) shows the annual mean residuals, far too spread out for independent errors, and panel (b) the two confidence bands.

exm-ggm-fgls-simulation.title: How many clusters are enough?
exm-ggm-fgls-simulation.html:
Simulate clusters of sizes 2,4,8 repeated 1,2,4,8,16,32 times, with a cluster-level regressor z, a within-cluster regressor w, and equicorrelation ρ=0.6 inside clusters. Estimate ρ by the analysis of variance moment estimator from the ordinary least squares residuals and form 𝛃β^F. Figure 31.4.1 shows 20,000 replications for each size.

The efficiency story is almost trivial. Ordinary least squares attains about 0.895 of the optimal precision for the coefficient of z — its variance is 1.12 times the optimal one — at every number of clusters, while feasible generalized least squares already reaches 0.987 with 3 clusters and 1.000 with 96. Estimating one smooth parameter costs almost nothing in efficiency, in sharp contrast with @exm-het-replicates, where a separate variance was estimated in each of ten groups.

The inference story is the opposite. The nominal 95% interval based on sF2(X⊤V(ρ^)−1X)−1 covers the truth in 0.728 of samples with 3 clusters, 0.916 with 12, and 0.944 with 96, while the interval that uses the true ρ covers 0.950 at three clusters and stays within simulation error of 95% at every size, as @thm-ggm-inference guarantees. The cluster-robust interval built on 𝛃β^F is uniformly a little better than the model-based one, but no cure when clusters are few — 0.764 at 3 — and the two become indistinguishable once there are several dozen, neither reaching the nominal level even at 96, where both stand at 0.944.

exm-ggm-nino-feasible.title: The El Niño trend without assuming \rho
exm-ggm-nino-feasible.title_html: The El Niño trend without assuming ρ
exm-ggm-nino-feasible.html: The analysis of @exm-ggm-elnino assumed ρ=0.5. The moment estimator from the ordinary least squares residuals gives ρ^=0.610, and the feasible generalized least squares fit then reports a trend of 0.1346 degrees per decade with standard error 0.0618. For comparison, the ordinary least squares trend, 0.1349, carries the usual standard error 0.0223 and a cluster-robust standard error of 0.0584 with years as clusters. The two honest routes agree closely and the naive one is out by a factor of nearly three. With 61 clusters both are in the range where @exm-ggm-fgls-simulation found them reliable.

exr-ggm-blue-subspace.title: C1
exr-ggm-blue-subspace.html: Let rank(X)=p and put 𝛌𝛌B={λ∈Rp:VX(X⊤X)−1λ∈C(X)}, the set of coefficient functions that ordinary least squares estimates best. Show that B is a subspace, that B=Rp iff C(VX)⊆C(X), and that dim⁡B=p−rank((I−M)VX(X⊤X)−1). Evaluate it for @exm-ggm-clusters.

exr-ggm-blup.title: C1
exr-ggm-blup.html: Suppose (Y⊤,Y0)⊤ is jointly distributed with 𝛃E(Y)=Xβ, 𝛃E(Y0)=x0⊤β, Cov(Y)=σ2V, Cov(Y,Y0)=σ2c and Var(Y0)=σ2v0, with V positive definite and rank(X)=p. Among predictors a⊤Y with E(a⊤Y−Y0)=0 for all 𝛃β, show that the one minimizing E(a⊤Y−Y0)2 is 𝛃𝛃Y^0=x0⊤β^V+c⊤V−1(Y−Xβ^V), with prediction error variance σ2[v0−c⊤V−1c+d⊤(X⊤V−1X)−1d], d=x0−X⊤V−1c. This is Goldberger’s formula; Chapter 32 recognizes it as the best linear unbiased predictor of a random effect.

exr-ggm-cluster-efficiency.title: B3
exr-ggm-cluster-efficiency.html: In @exm-ggm-clusters with two clusters of sizes m1 and m2, show that the efficiency of the sample mean as an estimate of the level is e=(m1+m2)2{(1−ρ)(m1+m2)+ρ(m12+m22)}(w1+w2),wk=mk1−ρ+mkρ. Show that e=1 when m1=m2, and find the limit as ρ→1 with m1=1 and m2=m.

exr-ggm-deterministic-row.title: B2
exr-ggm-deterministic-row.html: Suppose the first observation is measured without error, so V=(00⊤0V22) with V22 positive definite, and X=(x(1)⊤X2). Show that 𝛃x(1)⊤β is known exactly, and that the BLUE of any estimable 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β is the generalized least squares estimate from the remaining n−1 observations subject to the constraint x(1)⊤b=y1.

exr-ggm-drift-sharp.title: C1
exr-ggm-drift-sharp.html: Show that the bound of @lem-ggm-drift cannot be improved in order: construct a family with k=1, independent clusters of size 1, and a design for which 𝛆E‖n−1/2X⊤D(θ)ε‖2 is bounded below by a positive multiple of (θ−θ0)2.

exr-ggm-efficiency-flat.title: B3
exr-ggm-efficiency-flat.html: In the balanced cluster model of @exr-ggm-two-groups, all clusters of size m, consider estimating μ with weights built from a wrong value ρ1 when the truth is ρ0. Show that the resulting estimator is Y¯ for every ρ1, and hence that the efficiency is exactly 1. Contrast with the unbalanced case and explain the flat curve in Figure 31.4.1(a).

exr-ggm-eigen-columns.title: A1
exr-ggm-eigen-columns.html: Show directly from @thm-ggm-ols-blue(a)(v) that ordinary least squares is best when the columns of X are eigenvectors of V, and use this to recover the equicorrelation result of @exr-proj-equicorrelation.

exr-ggm-feasible-not-linear.title: A1
exr-ggm-feasible-not-linear.html: Explain why 𝛃β^F is not a linear function of Y, and why this alone makes @cor-opt-aitken inapplicable to it. Which part of @thm-ggm-inference could still hold exactly if 𝛉θ^ happened to be independent of Y?

exr-ggm-gls-unknown-theta.title: B2
exr-ggm-gls-unknown-theta.html: Suppose 𝛉Cov(Y)=Σ(θ) with 𝛉θ unknown, and that 𝛉C(Σ(θ)X)⊆C(X) for every 𝛉θ in the parameter set. Show that MY is a BLUE for every 𝛉θ, so that the best estimator is known even though the covariance is not. Give an example with two unknown variance components.

exr-ggm-gls-vs-ols-rss.title: B3
exr-ggm-gls-vs-ols-rss.html: Show that 𝛆𝛆𝛆𝛆ε^V⊤ε^V≥ε^⊤ε^, where 𝛆ε^=(I−M)y is the ordinary residual, with equality iff 𝛃Xβ^V=My. Show also that 𝛆𝛆𝛆𝛆ε^⊤V−1ε^≥ε^V⊤V−1ε^V. Explain why neither inequality says anything about which fit is better.

exr-ggm-known-blue-family.title: A2
exr-ggm-known-blue-family.html: Give a family 𝛉V(θ) with k=2 for which no estimation of 𝛉θ is needed to obtain the best estimator of 𝛃Xβ, and say what 𝛉θ is still needed for.

exr-ggm-lsce.title: C2
exr-ggm-lsce.html: Call 𝛃Xβ~ a least squares consistent estimate when it minimizes the ordinary sum of squares ‖y−Xb‖2 over F(y); this is the criterion used by Christensen (2020). Show that it agrees with @eq-ggm-projection-form when V is idempotent, and that in general the two differ. Show also that when C(VU)⊆C(U) the least squares consistent estimate is a BLUE.

exr-ggm-mle.title: C2
exr-ggm-mle.html: Let 𝛃𝛉Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2V(θ)) with rank(X)=p. Show that for each fixed 𝛉θ the log-likelihood is maximized over 𝛃(β,σ2) at 𝛃𝛉β^V(θ) and 𝛉𝛉σ^2(θ)=SSEV(θ)/n, and that the profile log-likelihood is 𝛉𝛉𝛉ℓp(θ)=−n2log⁡σ^2(θ)−12log⁡detV(θ)+const. Why does the determinant term make the normalization of V matter here, when @exr-ggm-scale says it does not matter for inference about 𝛃β?

exr-ggm-moment-rho.title: B1
exr-ggm-moment-rho.html: For balanced clusters of size m with equicorrelation ρ, let B and W be the between- and within-cluster mean squares of the ordinary least squares residuals. Show that the moment estimator ρ^=(B−W)/{B+(m−1)W} is the solution of matching EB and EW to their model values when the model is fitted without regressors, and explain why ρ^ can be negative. What does truncating it at zero do to @thm-ggm-feasible?

exr-ggm-multiple-of-i.title: A2
exr-ggm-multiple-of-i.html: Show that MV=VM for every X if and only if V is a multiple of I.

exr-ggm-oblique-leverage.title: B2
exr-ggm-oblique-leverage.html: Show that trAV=r for every positive definite V. Then take n=2, p=1, X=(12),V=(10.90.91), and show that the diagonal of AV is (−4/7,11/7). Why does this not contradict @prp-proj-leverage?

exr-ggm-plugin-bias.title: C2
exr-ggm-plugin-bias.html: Let 𝛉θ^ be independent of Y with 𝛉𝛉Eθ^=θ0, and write 𝛉𝛉g(θ)=a⊤(X⊤V(θ)−1X)−1a for the reported variance of 𝛃a⊤β^F at scale σ2=1, and 𝛉h(θ) for its true variance. Show that 𝛉𝛉h(θ)≥g(θ0) for every 𝛉θ, with equality at 𝛉θ0, and deduce that 𝛉Eg(θ^) understates 𝛉Eh(θ^) whenever g is concave near 𝛉θ0. Why does this not settle the question in general?

exr-ggm-quasi.title: B1
exr-ggm-quasi.html: Let V0=(1−ρ)Im+ρ11⊤ with −1/(m−1)<ρ<1. Verify @eq-ggm-equicorr-inverse by @thm-mat-woodbury, and show that L0=(Im−c11⊤/m)/1−ρ satisfies L0V0L0⊤=Im for c=1−(1−ρ)/(1+(m−1)ρ). Deduce @eq-ggm-quasi.

exr-ggm-rank-formula.title: A2
exr-ggm-rank-formula.html: Verify rank(X:V)=rank(X)+rank(V)−dim⁡(C(X)∩C(V)) and compute both sides for @exm-ggm-effects.

exr-ggm-residual-sum.title: A2
exr-ggm-residual-sum.html: Show that 𝛆1⊤ε^V=0 for every y iff 1∈C(V−1X). Give an example with an intercept in which this fails.

exr-ggm-scale.title: A1
exr-ggm-scale.html: Show that replacing (σ2,V) by (σ2/c,cV) for c>0 leaves 𝛃β^V, AV and every statistic in @thm-ggm-inference(d), (e) unchanged, and multiplies SSEV and sV2 by 1/c. Conclude that no normalization of V affects any inference about 𝛃β.

exr-ggm-shares.title: B1
exr-ggm-shares.html: Three fractions of a sample are measured and then rescaled so that they add to one. Model E(Yk)=μ+δk with ∑kδk=0 known, and suppose Cov(Y)=σ2(I3−11⊤/3). Which function of (μ,δ1,δ2) is known exactly? Find the variance of Y1−Y2 as an estimate of δ1−δ2, and explain why no other linear unbiased estimate exists.

exr-ggm-simple-structure.title: B1
exr-ggm-simple-structure.html: Assume the simple covariance structure V=XAX⊤+WBW⊤ of @thm-ggm-ols-blue(a)(iv). Show that Cov(MY,(I−M)Y)=0, and that the error can be written 𝛆𝛆𝛆ε=ε1+ε2 with 𝛆ε1∈C(X), 𝛆ε2∈C(X)⊥ and 𝛆𝛆Cov(ε1,ε2)=0 with probability one.

exr-ggm-singular-f.title: C1
exr-ggm-singular-f.html: In the setting of @thm-ggm-singular, let C(X0)⊆C(X) with ν0=rank(X0:V)−rank(X0) and ν=rank(X:V)−rank(X), and assume Y is normal and 𝛃Xβ∈C(X0:V). Working in the coordinates Z∗ of the proof of @thm-ggm-singular(f), show that SSEV,0−SSEV and SSEV are independent with (SSEV,0−SSEV)/σ2∼χ2(ν0−ν,γ), and identify γ. Why is the assumption 𝛃Xβ∈C(X0:V) needed?

exr-ggm-two-eigenvalues.title: C2
exr-ggm-two-eigenvalues.html: Suppose V has only two distinct eigenvalues, λ1 with multiplicity k and λ2 with multiplicity n−k, and let E1 be the eigenspace of λ1. Show that MV=VM iff C(X)=(C(X)∩E1)⊕(C(X)∩E1⊥). Deduce that when this splitting holds every 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^ has efficiency 1, and that when it fails there is a design attaining the bound 4λ1λ2/(λ1+λ2)2.

exr-ggm-two-groups.title: B4
exr-ggm-two-groups.html:
Observations Ykj, j=1,…,mk, k=1,…,G, have mean μ and covariance σ2V with V=(1−ρ)I+ρZZ⊤, Z the cluster indicator matrix. Using @eq-ggm-equicorr-inverse cluster by cluster, show that μ^V=∑kwkY¯k∑kwk,wk=mk1−ρ+mkρ,{#eq-ggm-cluster-weights}

with Var(μ^V)=σ2/∑kwk. Interpret the weights as ρ→0 and ρ→1.

exr-ggm-two-stage-weights.title: B2
exr-ggm-two-stage-weights.html: Suppose V(θ)=diag(1+θz1,…,1+θzn) with known zi≥0 and θ≥0. Verify (G1) and (G2) on a neighbourhood of an interior θ0, giving explicit constants, and show that (G3) holds when the zi and the rows of X are bounded.

exr-ggm-two-step-check.title: B3
exr-ggm-two-step-check.html: Verify directly from @eq-ggm-two-step that 𝛃Xβ~ does not depend on which generalized inverse K− is used, given y∈C(X:V).

exr-ggm-zero-variance.title: A1
exr-ggm-zero-variance.html: Show that if V is singular with Va=0, then a⊤Y is the same number for every possible data vector, and identify that number in terms of 𝛃β. What does this say about 𝛃a⊤Xβ when X⊤a=0?

lem-ggm-blue-criterion.title: Criterion for a BLUE
lem-ggm-blue-criterion.html:
Assume @eq-ggm-model with V nonnegative definite. Let c∈Rn and 𝛌λ=X⊤c, so that c⊤Y is a linear unbiased estimator of 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β.

  1. c⊤Y is a BLUE of 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β if and only if Vc∈C(X).

  2. Any two BLUEs of 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β are equal with probability one. More precisely, if c⊤Y and b⊤Y are both BLUEs then c⊤y=b⊤y for every y∈C(X:V).

  3. A matrix estimator AY with AX=X is a BLUE of 𝛃Xβ if and only if AV(I−M)=0, equivalently C(VA⊤)⊆C(X).

lem-ggm-colspace-sum.html: If A and B are nonnegative definite of the same order, then C(A+B)=C(A)+C(B).

lem-ggm-drift.title: The drift term for independent clusters
lem-ggm-drift.title_html: The drift term for independent clusters
lem-ggm-drift.html: Suppose the observations fall into G independent clusters of size at most m¯, that 𝛉V(θ) is block diagonal with one block per cluster for every 𝛉θ, and that (G1)–(G3) hold. Then for every fixed 𝛉θ∈B, 𝛉𝛆𝛉𝛉E‖n−1/2X⊤D(θ)ε‖2≤σ2m¯K2L2C‖θ−θ0‖2. In particular 𝛉𝛆𝛉𝛉n−1/2X⊤D(θ)ε=Op(‖θ−θ0‖).

prp-ggm-ols-loss.title: The cost of ordinary least squares
prp-ggm-ols-loss.title_html: The cost of ordinary least squares
prp-ggm-ols-loss.html:
Assume @eq-ggm-model with V positive definite and rank(X)=p. Write 𝛃β^=(X⊤X)−1X⊤Y and let λ1≥⋯≥λn>0 be the eigenvalues of V. For 𝛌λ≠0 define the efficiency 𝛌𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃e(λ)=Var(λ⊤β^V)/Var(λ⊤β^).

  1. 𝛃𝛃Cov(β^)−Cov(β^V) is nonnegative definite, so 𝛌0<e(λ)≤1 for every 𝛌λ.

  2. 𝛌e(λ)=1 if and only if 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^=λ⊤β^V with probability one, which by @thm-ggm-ols-blue(b) happens iff 𝛌VX(X⊤X)−1λ∈C(X).

  3. 𝛌e(λ)≥4λ1λn/(λ1+λn)2 for every 𝛌λ and every X, and the bound is attained.

thm-ggm-feasible.title: Feasible generalized least squares
thm-ggm-feasible.html:
Assume @eq-ggm-model with rank(X)=p fixed, and consider a sequence of models indexed by n. Suppose:

  • (G1) there are constants 0<c≤C<∞ and a neighbourhood B of 𝛉θ0 such that every eigenvalue of 𝛉V(θ) lies in [c,C] for all 𝛉θ∈B and all n;
  • (G2) 𝛉𝛉𝛉‖D(θ)‖2≤L‖θ−θ0‖ for 𝛉θ∈B, all n, with ‖⋅‖2 the spectral norm;
  • (G3) the rows of X satisfy ‖x(i)‖≤K, and n−1X⊤V−1X→A for a positive definite A;
  • (G4) 𝛉𝛉θ^→θ0 in probability.

Then:

  1. 𝛉n−1X⊤V(θ^)−1X→A in probability, so the reported covariance factor is consistent up to the scale σ2.

  2. If in addition 𝛉𝛉n(θ^−θ0)=Op(1) and

    • (G5) 𝛉𝛉𝛉𝛆sup‖θ−θ0‖≤δ ‖n−1/2X⊤D(θ)ε‖=Op(δ) as δ→0, uniformly in n,

    then 𝛃𝛃n(β^F−β^V)→0 in probability. Consequently 𝛃β^F has whatever limiting distribution 𝛃β^V has, and in particular 𝛃𝛃n(β^F−β)→Np(0,σ2A−1) whenever 𝛃𝛃n(β^V−β) does.

thm-ggm-inference.title: Inference under a known covariance shape
thm-ggm-inference.title_html: Inference under a known covariance shape
thm-ggm-inference.html:
Let 𝛃Y∼Nn(Xβ,σ2V) with V known and positive definite, r=rank(X)<n. Put 𝛆𝛆SSEV=ε^V⊤V−1ε^V=Y⊤V−1(I−AV)Y,sV2=SSEVn−r.{#eq-ggm-sse}

  1. For 𝛌λ∈C(X⊤), the statistic 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^V is the same for every solution of the generalized normal equations, and 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌λ⊤β^V∼N(λ⊤β, σ2λ⊤(X⊤V−1X)−λ). It is the best linear unbiased estimator of 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β (@cor-opt-aitken).

  2. SSEV/σ2∼χ2(n−r), independently of 𝛃Xβ^V.

  3. E(sV2)=σ2 and Var(sV2)=2σ4/(n−r).

  4. For estimable 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β with 𝛌λ≠0, 𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛃𝛌𝛌λ⊤β^V−λ⊤βsVλ⊤(X⊤V−1X)−λ∼t(n−r).

  5. Let C(X0)⊆C(X) with rank(X0)=r0<r, and let SSEV,0 be @eq-ggm-sse computed in the reduced model. Then F=(SSEV,0−SSEV)/(r−r0)sV2∼F(r−r0,n−r,γ),{#eq-ggm-f}

    with 𝛃γ=‖(M∗−M∗0)X∗β‖2/σ2, where M∗ and M∗0 are the orthogonal projections onto C(V−1/2X) and C(V−1/2X0). The noncentrality is zero iff 𝛃Xβ∈C(X0).

thm-ggm-ols-blue.title: When ordinary least squares is best
thm-ggm-ols-blue.title_html: When ordinary least squares is best
thm-ggm-ols-blue.html:
Assume @eq-ggm-model with V nonnegative definite, and let W be any n×(n−r) matrix with C(W)=C(X)⊥.

  1. The following are equivalent.

    1. MY is a BLUE of 𝛃Xβ.
    2. MV(I−M)=0, equivalently MV=VM.
    3. C(VX)⊆C(X).
    4. V=XAX⊤+WBW⊤ for some nonnegative definite A and B.
    5. C(X) has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of V.

  2. For 𝛒ρ∈Rn, the estimator 𝛒ρ⊤MY of 𝛒𝛃ρ⊤Xβ is a BLUE if and only if 𝛒VMρ∈C(X). When rank(X)=p and 𝛌λ∈Rp, this reads 𝛌VX(X⊤X)−1λ∈C(X).

  3. If V is positive definite, the conditions of (a) are also equivalent to My=AVy for every y, and then ordinary and generalized least squares give the same fit, the same estimate of every estimable function, and the same SSEV.

thm-ggm-singular.title: The general Gauss–Markov model
thm-ggm-singular.html:
Assume @eq-ggm-model with V nonnegative definite of rank q.

  1. (Consistency.) 𝛃N⊤Y=N⊤Xβ with probability one; consequently Pr(Y∈C(X:V))=1 and 𝛃Pr(Xβ∈Y+C(V))=1.

  2. (Estimability and perfect estimation.) 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β has a linear unbiased estimator iff 𝛌λ∈C(X⊤), exactly as when V=I. It has a linear unbiased estimator of variance zero iff 𝛌λ∈C(X⊤N), a subspace of dimension r−d, and then 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β=b⊤N⊤Y with probability one for any b with 𝛌X⊤Nb=λ.

  3. (Rao’s unified formula.) Let T=V+XX⊤. Then C(T)=C(X:V), TT+X=X, and A=X(X⊤T+X)−X⊤T+{#eq-ggm-rao}

    satisfies AX=X and AV(I−M)=0. Hence AY is a BLUE of 𝛃Xβ.

  4. (Uniqueness.) Every estimable 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β has a BLUE, and any two BLUEs of it agree for every y∈C(X:V), hence with probability one.

  5. (Projection form.) Let y∈C(X:V). The set F(y)={b:y−Xb∈C(V)} is nonempty, and 𝛃β~∈argminb∈F(y) (y−Xb)⊤V+(y−Xb){#eq-ggm-projection-form}

    determines 𝛃Xβ~ uniquely; the map 𝛃y↦Xβ~ is linear and 𝛃Xβ~ is a BLUE of 𝛃Xβ. Explicitly, with K=N⊤X and any generalized inverse K−, 𝛃Xβ~=Xb∗+U(U⊤V+U)−1U⊤V+(y−Xb∗),b∗=K−N⊤y.{#eq-ggm-two-step}

  6. (Error sum of squares.) Put 𝛆𝛃ε^=Y−Xβ~ and 𝛆𝛆SSEV=ε^⊤V+ε^. Then E(SSEV)=σ2(q−d), and q−d=rank(X:V)−rank(X). If Y is normal, then SSEV/σ2∼χ2(q−d), independently of 𝛃Xβ~.
